title: Bluff Round
tagline: Make up an answer good enough to fool the table. Then find the real one.
howTo: Everyone types a fake answer to the question.
The fakes are mixed with the truth. Pick the one you think is real.
1,000 points for finding the truth. 500 for every person your fake fools.

questions.question: A group of turkeys is called a ____.
The fleshy red flap that hangs over a turkey's beak is called a ____.
The Beatles song "Yesterday" started out with the working title ____.
questions.fact: Paul McCartney sang "Scrambled eggs, oh my baby how I love your legs" until he found real words.

questions.question: Pink Floyd took their name from two blues musicians: Pink Anderson and ____.
When President Franklin Roosevelt moved Thanksgiving a week earlier in 1939, critics nicknamed the new holiday ____.
Before it was renamed for an Olympic legend, the Pennsylvania town of Jim Thorpe was called ____.
Punxsutawney Phil's full title is "Seer of Seers, Sage of Sages, Prognosticator of Prognosticators and ____".
Pennsylvania's official state toy is the ____.
questions.fact: The Slinky was invented in Philadelphia in the 1940s.

questions.question: The Big Mac was invented in 1967 by a McDonald's owner in the Pennsylvania town of ____.
questions.fact: Jim Delligatti created it at his Uniontown restaurant, about an hour south of Pittsburgh.

questions.question: Sarah Josepha Hale, who spent years campaigning to make Thanksgiving a national holiday, also wrote the nursery rhyme ____.
Ohio's flag is the only U.S. state flag that is not a ____.
questions.fact: Ohio's flag is a swallowtail shape called a burgee.

questions.question: The banana split was invented in 1904 in the Pennsylvania town of ____.
In the Beatles song "Rocky Raccoon", Rocky checks into his room and finds a copy of ____.
The buckeye nut got its name because it looks like the eye of a ____.
questions.fact: A buck is a male deer, hence buck-eye.
